h: Each Soul Finds Its Own Lamp in the Torah

p: נֵר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז)
"The lamp of Hashem is the soul of man" (Mishlei 20:27).
וְאִיתָא בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צד, ב)
And it is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 94b):
And the neshamah is from above,
and there is no bad or blemish in it
Shaar HaYirah chapter 9, from the Tikkunim);
"My God, the soul You placed within me
And the assembly of the souls of Yisrael
וְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ נֵר מְיוּחָד
and every soul has a lamp of its own:
And the Torah too is a lamp:
and it is "a lamp to my feet is Your word,
and a light to my path" (Tehillim 119:105);
has a portion in the Torah,
For so it was in the generation of the wilderness:
and corresponding to them six hundred thousand letters in the Torah,
"there are six hundred thousand letters in the Torah";
and although the count is not exact,
and this is the Written Torah.
And afterward, with the novellae of Torah,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַדֵּשׁ הֲלָכָה בְּכׇל יוֹם
for Hashem Yisbarach innovates a halachah every day
And this is why we request:
"and grant our portion in Your Torah";
has a portion in the Torah,
"The lamp of Hashem is the soul of man."
all the desire of this world,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת (כְּתוּבּוֹת קד, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל לֹא)
as Tosafos wrote (Kesubos 104, the passage beginning "Lo")
in the name of a Midrash:
that words of Torah enter his body,
let him pray that there not enter
(וְעַיֵּין תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק כו
(and see Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu Rabbah chapter 26
וְלֹא נוּכַל לְקַיֵּים כׇּל מִצְוֹת ה׳
And we cannot fulfill all of Hashem's mitzvos
that Shabbos is equal to the entire Torah;
וּבְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, א)
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 92a):
is like one who keeps the whole Torah."
and through this we can request,
"and grant our portion in Your Torah,"
that each of us attain his portion in the Torah,
as it will be in the future,
"And they will not teach, each man," etc.,
from the smallest of them to the greatest";
for the main point of all learning
is to understand and to know
the utterance "I am Hashem your God,"
which is the sum of the entire Torah.
And since they will all know Hashem,
they will not need instructors and teachers,
and each will learn from his own lamp:
"A lamp to my feet is Your word,
and a light to my path."
at the end of the offerings
"that the Beis HaMikdash be rebuilt speedily in our days,
and grant our portion in Your Torah";
which stands in place of an offering
"the prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily offerings"),
and "let us render bulls with our lips" (Hoshea 14:3),
the rebuilding of the Beis HaMikdash,
and that there shine to each one of Yisrael
which is equal to all the mitzvos,
"and grant our portion in Your Torah";
for through the mitzvah of Shabbos
to each one his portion in His Torah.
"In returning and rest you shall be saved";
and "rest" is the rest of Shabbos.
"It is good to give thanks (lehodos) to Hashem,"
"One who confesses (modeh) and forsakes will find mercy."
at the meal of the Field of Apples,
and it is stated in the holy Zohar
above the letters of the holy Name,
for they are of the daytime,"
that there shine to each one of Yisrael
his own lamp in the Torah,
in the manner of the future,
"a lamp to my feet is Your word,
and a light to my path."
